Campaign.title: Campaign
Campaign.description: A campaign that can be sent to a list of recipients

start_date.description: Start date in YYYY-MM-DD format. Uses the campaign's timezone.

end_date.description: End date in YYYY-MM-DD format. Uses the campaign's timezone.

sequences.description: List of sequences (the actual email copy). Even though this field is an array, only the first element is used, so please provide only one array item, and add the steps to that array

steps.description: The steps of the sequence. Each sequence needs at least one step.

type.description: Type of step. This has to be 'email' always - it's the only supported type for now

delay.description: The delay value before sending the NEXT email. The unit is determined by the delay_unit field (defaults to days). The total delay cannot exceed 366 days.

delay_unit.description: The unit of time for the delay value (minutes, hours, or days). Defaults to days for backward compatibility.

pre_delay.description: The delay value before sending the FIRST email in a subsequence. **Only applicable to subsequences** - this field is ignored for regular campaigns. The unit is determined by the pre_delay_unit field (defaults to days). The total delay cannot exceed 366 days.

pre_delay_unit.description: The unit of time for the pre_delay value (minutes, hours, or days). **Only applicable to subsequences** - this field is ignored for regular campaigns. Defaults to days for backward compatibility.

Email.title: Email
Email.description: A campaign email, a reply, a manually sent email, or any other email that's visible in the Unibox

timestamp_created.description: Timestamp when the email was added to our database. This is not the timestamp of the email itself, since the email could have been sent at a different time. Please check the `timestamp_email` field for the timestamp of the email.

timestamp_email.description: The timestamp of the email, as provided by the email server. Please note that the timestamp is not always accurate, as it can be manipulated by the sender or the email server.

message_id.description: Unique email ID from the email server

subject.description: Subject line of the email message

from_address_email.description: The sender email address, populated based on the eaccount

to_address_email_list.description: Comma-separated list of recipient email addresses

cc_address_email_list.description: Comma-separated list of CC email addresses

bcc_address_email_list.description: Comma-separated list of BCC email addresses

body.description: An object containing the email body in HTML and text format

text.description: Plain-text representation of the email body. Newline characters are preserved as line breaks in this text view.

html.description:
HTML content of the email. Use `
` tags for delivered email line breaks.
html.example:
This is a test email.

Second line.

campaign_id.description: The id of the campaign that the email is associated with (it can be null for manually sent emails)

subsequence_id.description: The id of the campaign subsequence that the email is associated with (it can be null for manually sent emails)

list_id.description: The id of the list (if the lead is part of a list)

lead.description: The email address of the lead that the email is associated with

eaccount.description: The email account that was used to send the email. This needs to be validated to make sure it exists in the user workspace

ue_type.description: Email type based on the life cycle of the email

step.description: The campaign step that the email is associated with

is_unread.description: Indicates if the email is unread

is_auto_reply.description: Indicates if the email is an auto-reply. 0 (zero) - is false, and 1 is true

ai_assisted.description: Indicates if AI assistance was used

is_focused.description: Indicates if the email is focused (is in the primary tab in the Unibox)

i_status.description: Indicates the interest status of the email

thread_id.description: Identifier for the email thread. All the emails in the same thread have the same thread ID

content_preview.description: A short preview of the email content (usually the first few lines of the email)
content_preview.example: This is a preview of the email content.

body_fallback_reason.description: Set only when `body` is not the full email body. `too_large`: the body was too large to include in a list response. `unavailable`: the body could not be read for this response. get.description:
Get analytics overview for one or multiple campaigns. Specify the `id` field to get the analytics overview for a single campaign, or leave it empty to get the analytics overview for all campaigns.

Note regarding the interest status totals (interested, meeting booked, meeting completed, closed): these are calculated based on the first occurrence of each event per contact by default. To change this behavior and calculate the totals based on all occurrences of the events, set the `expand_crm_events` parameter to `true`. Additionally, there is a 10 minute time window after you change a lead status in which the subsequent updates will NOT insert new analytics events to avoid duplicates from rapid status changes and avoid false inflation of the analytics numbers.

Example: if a lead goes from interested to meeting booked to closed, it will count as 3 events (total_interested: 1, total_meeting_booked_1, and total_closed: 1) when this parameter is set to true, and as 1 event (total_interested) when it is set to false (default).

post.description:
This endpoint is a POST endpoint, instead of GET - a deviation from the REST APIs standards we’re following because of the complex arguments it accepts, which would be too hard to express through query parameters. Results are ordered by each lead's `id` field in ascending order (or by `contact` when distinct_contacts is true) so clients can paginate chronologically by reusing the cursor returned in `next_starting_after`. Leads created on or after October 15, 2025 respect this chronological ordering; older records may appear out of sequence when sorted by ID.


Requires one of the following scopes: `leads:read`, `leads:all`, `all:read`, `all:all`

search.description: Search term matched against the lead's email and profile fields (first and last name, company, job title, and similar). Matches whole words, and the beginning of a field's value — "smith" finds "John Smith", "mith" does not. Provide `campaign` or `list_id` to also match inside values. Newly created or updated leads can take a few seconds to become searchable.

post.summary: Add leads in bulk to a campaign or list
post.description:
Adds up to 1000 leads to either a campaign or a list. You must provide a `campaign_id` or a `list_id`, but not both. The endpoint validates emails, checks against blocklists and existing leads.


Requires one of the following scopes: `leads:create`, `leads:all`, `all:create`, `all:all`

campaign_id.description: The unique identifier for the campaign to add leads to. Use this field OR `list_id`, but not both.

list_id.description: The unique identifier for the list to add leads to. Use this field OR `campaign_id`, but not both.

leads.description: An array of lead objects to create. When using `campaign_id`: Each lead object must contain an `email`. When using `list_id` Each lead object must contain at least one of the following: `email`, `first_name`, or `last_name`.

lt_interest_status.description: Lead interest status. It can be either a static value (check below), or a custom status interest value

assigned_to.description: ID of the user assigned to the lead

custom_variables.description: Custom variables can include any metadata about the lead that is relevant to the campaign, the campaign will be updated to allow all the other leads in the campaign to have the same custom variables. The custom variables will be added to the lead payload field

blocklist_id.description: Optional. Leads are always checked against your workspace blocklist; any other blocklist ID is ignored.

assigned_to.description: Optional user ID to assign all imported leads to. If omitted, leads are assigned to the campaign owner when `campaign_id` is defined, or the user making the request.

verify_leads_on_import.description: If true, a background job will be created to verify the email addresses of the imported leads.

skip_if_in_workspace.description: If true, any lead that already exists anywhere in your workspace (in any campaign or list) will be skipped. This option overrides the other "skip_if" flags.

skip_if_in_campaign.description: If true, any lead that already exists in ANY campaign in your workspace will be skipped.

skip_if_in_list.description: If true, any lead that already exists in ANY list in your workspace will be skipped.

idempotency_key.description: Optional. Makes retries safe: a retry with the same key and the same leads to the same campaign or list does not insert the leads again, and reports the leads it already created in `created_leads` and `leads_uploaded`. A key is permanent: use a new one for every batch. A lead is recognised by its position in `leads` and its email (or name), so resend the same array.

200.description: A summary of the bulk import operation.

schema.description: A summary of the bulk import operation.

total_sent.description: The total number of leads included in the request payload.

leads_uploaded.description: The number of leads that were successfully created.

in_blocklist.description: The number of leads that were skipped because their email was found on the blocklist.

blocklist_used.description: The ID of the blocklist that was used for the check.

duplicated_leads.description: The number of leads that were already in this specific campaign or list and were not re-added.

skipped_count.description: The number of leads skipped due to the `skip_if_in_...` flags being enabled.

invalid_email_count.description: The number of leads skipped due to an invalid email format or a missing email address.

incomplete_count.description: The number of leads skipped due to missing email and names. Only calculated for lists.

duplicate_email_count.description: The number of leads skipped because their email was duplicated within the request payload itself.

remaining_in_plan.description: The remaining lead uploads in the current billing plan. This value is only present in the response when a `campaign_id` is provided.

created_leads.description: A list of created leads with their summary information. You can use this to map your input to the created leads.

index.description: The index of the lead in the input array. For leads that have no email address you can use this field as the key to your input leads.

id.description: The ID of the lead. Use it for GET, DELETE or PATCH operations.
